quote: 14.1 Indemnification by RevMed. RevMed shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Sanofi, its Affiliates and their respective officers, directors, agents and employees ("Sanofi Indemnitees") from and against any Third Party Claims and Losses arising therefrom under or related to this Agreement against any of them to the extent arising or resulting from:

There is no indemnity for third-party claims that RevMed's services, deliverables or licensed technology infringe or misappropriate intellectual property, none for RevMed's breach of Applicable Law, and none for RevMed-caused unauthorised access to or disclosure of our data; Section 13.5 disclaims any non-infringement warranty, so 14.1(b) does not fill the gap (an indemnity is claim allocation, not a warranty). Our own indemnity (14.2) is far broader than the narrow Customer indemnity the playbook permits. We add limbs (d)-(f) and narrow 14.2 to Sanofi-provided content and Sanofi's breach of Applicable Law, closing the list cleanly at (b). We deliberately leave the exception chapeau tied to limbs "(a) through (c)", so the Sanofi-fault carve-outs do not reach the new limbs. There are no volume caps on Sanofi, no shortfall or penalty mechanic, and no committed minimum spend: the Research Budget is an estimate governed by the JSC/JRDC and, from CY2021 onward, subject to Sanofi's final decision-making power (§4.2(a)(ii)-(iii)). Manufacturing/supply is left to a future Supply Agreement to be negotiated (§7.3) with no requirements or minimum-order term, and the only purchase obligation on termination falls on RevMed (§12.5 inventory purchase), which benefits us. Sanofi also retains termination for convenience in its entirety or country/Product-by-Product (§12.2(a)(i)), providing a clean exit. No redline required.

quote: 12.1 Term. The term of this Agreement shall commence upon the Effective Date and, unless earlier terminated pursuant to this Article XII, shall continue in full force and effect until the expiration of Sanofi's payment obligations under Article IX or the Profit/Loss Share Agreement, whichever is later (the "Term").
rationale: This is a collaboration/licence agreement with no renewal mechanic at all. Section 12.1 sets a single Term that runs to the expiration of Sanofi's payment obligations under Article IX or the Profit/Loss Share Agreement (which are in turn bounded by the Royalty Term in Section 9.3(b)), subject only to early termination under Article XII. Targeted searches for "renew", "automatically renew", "successive/additional term", "unless either Party gives written notice prior to expiration", and price-uplift/CPI language returned no auto-renewal, no non-renewal notice window, and no renewal price-increase mechanic (the only "renewal" hits are patent continuations and insurance non-renewal notice, neither of which is a term renewal). Because there is no automatic renewal, the conditional preferred and fallback elements (renewal term length, opt-out window, Vendor reminder, and price-increase caps) are not triggered, and any extension of the Term would require the Parties' mutual agreement. The clause therefore creates no lock-in or notice-window trap for us, and there is nothing to redline; the rule is structurally inapplicable to this deal.

rationale: Article XII's exit machinery runs one way: Section 12.3(c)(vi) and 12.3(c)(iv)/(v) oblige Sanofi to provide transition assistance and transfer regulatory materials, data, marks and inventory to RevMed. Nothing obliges RevMed to give Sanofi transition assistance or to export Sanofi's data on expiry or termination generally; Section 12.3(e) (p0531) is limited to one Change-of-Control scenario, and Section 11.6 only provides for destruction of Confidential Information on request, not return/export within a fixed period. ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: New Section 12.3(f): "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, RevMed shall..." — covers both expiry and any termination, and is not limited to a Change-of-Control or Termination Product scenario.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: The inserted clause provides assistance "for a period of at least ninety (90) days"; there is no six-month (or longer) assistance period. To reach preferred, change to "for a period of up to six (6) months following such expiration or termination".

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3(f) is silent on pricing for the assistance; no "at RevMed's then-current rates" (or any charging basis) appears. Preferred requires an express rate anchor.

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "shall, within thirty (30) days after such expiration or termination, export and deliver to Sanofi all data and materials of Sanofi then in RevMed's possession or control" — 30-day clock runs from expiry/termination, not from a request.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: No format requirement in the inserted sentence; the only electronic-format reference is in 12.3(c)(vi)C, which runs from Sanofi to RevMed. Add "in a commonly used, machine-readable format".

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: No deletion-and-certification obligation was inserted. Section 11.6 only requires destruction of Confidential Information on a party's written request (with archival/backup retention carve-outs) and is not tied to occur after return/export, so it does not supply this element.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason" — the assistance period and the export duty both attach to every covered expiry or termination event, satisfying the requirement that the period apply after every covered exit.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: "provide Sanofi with reasonable transition assistance for a period of at least ninety (90) days following such expiration or termination" — RevMed (counterparty) is the obligor and the floor is 90 days. The "at Sanofi's request" trigger is a general request condition, not one tied only to anticipated expiry.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "shall, within thirty (30) days after such expiration or termination, export and deliver to Sanofi all data and materials of Sanofi then in RevMed's possession or control" — unconditional, correct temporal anchor, correct party direction.

verification.notes: Position-complete at the fallback: all three fallback elements are met in operative language (90-day floor, 30-day export, applies to any expiry or termination, obligor is RevMed). Preferred is not met — the clause lacks the six-month period, the then-current-rates anchor, the machine-readable format requirement, and the post-return certified-deletion step. The finding's 'missing' classification is sound: existing 12.3(c)(vi)/(vi)C impose transition and transfer duties only on Sanofi; 12.3(e) is confined to one Change-of-Control termination scenario with bracketed, undisclosed scope; and 11.6 provides only request-based destruction of Confidential Information, not a fixed-period return/export to Sanofi. Minimality holds: a single concise sentence inserted as 12.3(f), nothing deleted or paraphrased elsewhere, no survival tail, expense allocation, procedure or boilerplate added. Note for the drafter: "and materials" marginally exceeds the data-export element; trimming to "all Sanofi data" would be tighter, but the phrase is a single deliverable formulation in this context and does not amount to a separate added requirement. Intent preserved: the insertion is additive and reciprocal, uses only defined parties, creates no undefined term or dangling cross-reference, and does not contradict 12.3(e) (narrow CoC assistance) or 11.6 (which continues to govern destruction of Confidential Information on request). If the client wants the preferred position, the repair is limited to four edits in 12.3(f): extend to "up to six (6) months", add "at RevMed's then-current rates", add "in a commonly used, machine-readable format" to the export obligation, and add "and shall thereafter delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing" (sequenced after return).

ops.text: RevMed warrants that (i) any software delivered by RevMed to Sanofi under this Agreement will conform in all material respects to its documentation for ninety (90) days following delivery, and (ii) the services RevMed performs under this Agreement will conform in all material respects to the applicable Research Plan or Development Plan for thirty (30) days following performance. quote: 13.5 No Other Warranties. EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY STATED IN THIS ARTICLE XIII, (A) NO REPRESENTATION, CONDITION OR WARRANTY WHATSOEVER IS MADE OR GIVEN BY OR ON BEHALF OF SANOFI OR REVMED; AND (B) ALL OTHER CONDITIONS AND WARRANTIES WHETHER WRITTEN OR ORAL OR EXPRESS OR IMPLIED ARE HEREBY EXPRESSLY EXCLUDED, INCLUDING ANY CONDITIONS AND WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE OR NON-INFRINGEMENT.
rationale: Article XIII contains only title/IP-style representations given as of the Execution Date (13.1, 13.2) and covenants (13.3, 13.4); nowhere in the Agreement is there a performance warranty for RevMed's work — no conformance warranty for any software or deliverable, no warranted period for RevMed's services, and no repair/replacement or refund remedy (searches for "software", "Deliverable" and workmanlike/performance standards return nothing). Section 13.5 then disclaims everything not expressly stated in Article XIII, so the gap is affirmative rather than merely silent, which fails every fallback element. We therefore insert the shortest fallback warranty as new Section 13.3(e) — 90-day software-to-documentation conformance, 30-day services conformance, with repair/replacement or refund — placed inside Article XIII so the 13.5 carve-out preserves it. We did not pursue the preferred 12-month/no-malicious-code package; compliance with Applicable Law is already covered by the mutual covenant in Section 13.4(b).

elements.evidence: The inserted paragraph warrants only that services "will conform in all material respects to the applicable Research Plan or Development Plan for thirty (30) days following performance"; no professional-and-workmanlike/industry-standard performance standard appears anywhere in Article XIII.

verification.notes: Fallback checklist is complete on the operative text: an express software-to-documentation warranty at exactly the 90-day floor, an express 30-day services conformance warranty, and both repair/replacement (plus re-performance) and refund remedies in a single sentence. Preferred level is not reached: no professional-and-workmanlike standard, software period is 90 days rather than 12 months, services period is 30 days rather than 90, no malicious-code warranty, and compliance with Applicable Law is only asserted (Section 13.4(b)) rather than shown in the rendered text. Minimality holds: the redline is a pure insertion placed inside Article XIII, deletes nothing, adds no survival tail, expense allocation, notice procedure, cure period, or extra damages categories, and adds no requirement outside the fallback checklist. Re-performance is a natural variant of the repair/replace remedy for services, not a separate obligation on Vendor beyond the checklist. Intent is preserved: Section 13.5 carves out anything "EXPRESSLY STATED IN THIS ARTICLE XIII," so siting the new warranty in Article XIII keeps it outside the disclaimer without editing 13.5; the existing representations, covenants 13.3(a)-(d) and the mutual disclaimer survive without contradiction. Drafting nit (not a failure): the inserted paragraph follows the 13.3 lead-in "RevMed covenants to Sanofi that:" but is a free-standing sentence rather than a lettered subsection; number it expressly (e.g., new Section 13.3(e) or a new Section 13.4A) so it plainly reads as an Article XIII warranty and not as an orphan continuation of the covenant list. Also confirm that "Development Plan" (and "Research Plan") are defined terms in the Agreement; if "Development Plan" is undefined, the services conformance benchmark would rest on an undefined trigger and should be replaced with a defined plan reference or a professional-and-workmanlike standard.

quote: 14.6 Insurance. Each Party shall procure and maintain insurance, including product liability insurance, with respect to its activities hereunder and under the Ancillary Agreements and which is consistent with normal business practices of companies similarly situated
rationale: Clause 14.6 is the only insurance provision in the Agreement. It obliges each Party (including RevMed) to carry insurance, including product liability, but sets no monetary limits and no E&O or cyber/privacy coverage; "consistent with normal business practices" is not a quantified floor. It therefore fails the fallback, which requires professional errors and omissions coverage of at least USD 1,000,000 and cyber and privacy coverage of at least USD 2,000,000. We proposed the shortest fix: a new 14.7 imposing those two fallback minimums on RevMed, leaving 14.6's evidence-on-request, notice and self-insurance mechanics intact (14.6's evidence-upon-request sentence already covers certificates, but that is a preferred-level element and is not relied on here).

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: Neither retained 14.6 ("insurance, including product liability insurance ... consistent with normal business practices") nor the inserted paragraph states any CGL per-occurrence limit; the insertion covers only E&O and cyber.

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: No aggregate CGL figure appears anywhere in 14.6 or the new "Insurance Minimums" paragraph.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted language sets E&O at "not less than USD 1,000,000", which is the fallback floor, not the preferred USD 2,000,000.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted language sets cyber liability at "not less than USD 2,000,000", below the preferred USD 5,000,000 trigger amount.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: No workers' compensation obligation appears in 14.6 or in the inserted paragraph.

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: Retained 14.6: "Each Party shall provide the other Party with evidence of such insurance upon request" — an evidence-on-request mechanic binding RevMed in Sanofi's favour (note: "such insurance" is anchored to 14.6, so it does not expressly reach the new minimums).

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted paragraph: "RevMed shall maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000" — express, unconditional, and directed at the counterparty.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted paragraph: "... and cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000"; "cyber liability" matches the playbook's cyber/privacy coverage wording used in the model language.

verification.notes: Position-complete at the fallback level: both fallback elements (E&O USD 1,000,000 and cyber USD 2,000,000) are met by a single inserted sentence binding RevMed, the party that bears the one-way insurance-notice obligation to Sanofi in 14.6 and is therefore the counterparty for this rule. Preferred level fails on four elements: no CGL per-occurrence or aggregate limits, E&O at 1M rather than 2M, cyber at 2M rather than 5M, and no workers' compensation obligation. Certificates-on-request is the only preferred element carried by retained 14.6. Minimal: the insertion adds exactly the two fallback coverages at exactly the fallback thresholds, with no survival tail, no "at its own expense", no certificate procedure, and no term anchor drawn from the model language. Nothing in 14.6 is deleted or paraphrased, so the self-insurance right, the notice period and the no-limit-on-indemnification sentence all survive. Preserves intent: the new floor operates alongside 14.6's "consistent with normal business practices" standard without contradiction, and creates no undefined term or dangling cross-reference. Note for the drafter only (not a defect at the selected level): because 14.6's evidence-on-request sentence refers to "such insurance", it is arguably confined to 14.6 coverage; if the team later pursues the preferred certificates element, tie the new paragraph to that sentence or add "certificates of insurance on request" expressly. No repair is required for the claimed fallback target; the finding is correctly classified as a deviation with an insertion remedy.
